rules.statement: Maintain each configuration fact once in the layer that owns it; do not put engine flags in profiles, model paths in engine files, or duplicate model sampling defaults. Shared instance configuration must not duplicate operating-system-specific runtime paths; launchers should supply machine-local binary and model roots explicitly, with environment variables only as documented optional fallbacks. Backend-specific process environment such as GPU-selection variables belongs in the engine configuration and is applied by Dispatcher when it launches llama.cpp rather than being required in the caller's shell. Instance repositories under `instances/<name>/` are user-owned independent Git repositories: Dispatcher core ignores their contents and must not register or manage them as Git submodules.
rules.title: Keep configuration in its owning layer
rules.why: Clear ownership prevents conflicting configuration, repeated maintenance, and hidden ambient startup state.

rules.statement: Configuration is deep-merged in this order: model defaults, instance engine defaults, profile, ensemble model entry; ad-hoc llama.cpp CLI overrides have highest priority.
rules.title: Configuration precedence
rules.why: A deterministic precedence order makes the effective llama.cpp configuration predictable.

rules.statement: Manage dependencies with uv rather than direct pip, conda, or poetry commands, and run tests or project executions through uv run.
rules.title: Use uv for project dependency and execution workflows
rules.why: The project uses one dependency and execution workflow to keep environments consistent.

rules.statement: Strictly separate observed, declared, and unknown facts.
rules.title: Separate observed, declared, and unknown facts
rules.why: Implementation and documentation should not turn assumptions into asserted project facts.

rules.statement: Configuration describes intent; code implements it, never the other way around.
rules.title: Configuration states intent
rules.why: Runtime transformation should follow explicit configuration instead of hidden code-side policy.

rules.statement: Prefer small, understandable changes.
rules.title: Prefer small understandable changes
rules.why: Small coherent changes are easier to review, test, and reason about.

rules.statement: Normalize parameter keys by removing leading dashes, replacing underscores with dashes, and mapping known shorthands or aliases to canonical long forms without leading dashes.
rules.title: Canonicalize parameter names
rules.why: One canonical representation prevents silent mismatches across defaults, profiles, ensembles, CLI input, and telemetry.

rules.statement: Add new llama.cpp parameters to PARAM_MAPPING in dispatcher.py when shorthand or spelling canonicalization is required.
rules.title: Register new llama.cpp parameters
rules.why: The mapping is the explicit source for translating accepted aliases into canonical parameter names.

rules.statement: For parameters configured by the selected alias, Dispatcher policy overwrites client values; request parameters not managed by that alias pass through unchanged.
rules.title: Dispatcher policy overrides managed client values
rules.why: Central configuration must be authoritative without blocking unrelated OpenAI-compatible or future llama.cpp request fields.

rules.statement: When chat_template_kwargs is configured for an alias, replace the client object with the configured object rather than recursively merging it.
rules.title: Replace chat_template_kwargs as one policy value
rules.why: The runtime treats chat_template_kwargs as one Dispatcher policy value.

rules.statement: Preserve client intent before transformation and log the request resolution and effective values after policy enforcement and optional target remapping.
rules.title: Preserve and log request transformation
rules.why: Telemetry must show both what the client requested and what llama.cpp actually received.

rules.statement: Exclude messages, prompt, and input from proxy parameter snapshots while retaining request control parameters.
rules.title: Do not duplicate prompt content in proxy telemetry
rules.why: Telemetry should capture request controls without duplicating conversation or prompt content.

rules.statement: In ensemble operation, clients must connect to the Dispatcher proxy rather than directly to the internal llama.cpp server.
rules.title: Clients must use the Dispatcher proxy
rules.why: Direct llama.cpp access bypasses virtual aliases, Dispatcher parameter injection, alias remapping, and proxy telemetry.

rules.statement: Do not modify an execution_runs record after it has been written.
rules.title: Execution runs are immutable historical headers
rules.why: execution_runs is the historical run header.

rules.statement: Record exactly one serve_model_instance even in Single Profile Mode.
rules.title: Record a runtime model instance in every mode
rules.why: Evaluations remain homogeneous between single-profile and ensemble modes.

rules.statement: Validate external FastAPI endpoint payloads with Pydantic models or explicit validation.
rules.title: Validate FastAPI payloads
rules.why: External request data must be checked before it enters orchestration logic.

rules.statement: Do not use blocking calls such as time.sleep or subprocess.run in the orchestrator; start subprocesses and consume their logs asynchronously.
rules.title: Keep orchestration non-blocking
rules.why: Blocking calls would stall the asynchronous service.

rules.statement: metrics_bench.speed_error is mandatory.
rules.title: Benchmark speed error is mandatory
rules.why: Benchmark measurements should carry their uncertainty.

rules.statement: metrics_eval.perplexity_error is mandatory where available.
rules.title: Perplexity error is mandatory when available
rules.why: Evaluation measurements should carry their uncertainty when it can be computed.

rules.statement: Do not record a measurement without an error value when repetitions are available.
rules.title: Repeated measurements require an error value
rules.why: Repeated measurements provide the information needed to report uncertainty.

rules.statement: Make new features testable first with --compile-only or /debug/preview where applicable.
rules.title: Make new behavior previewable before full operation
rules.why: Configuration and request transformations should be inspectable before a full runtime path is exercised.

rules.statement: For schema evolution, avoid destructive updates to existing measurement data, use PRAGMA user_version, and map migrations in a controlled manner in database_manager.py.
rules.title: Future schema evolution safeguards
rules.why: Measurement history must remain trustworthy across future schema changes.

rules.statement: Store parameter names in canonical dashed form in the database, but write OpenAI-compatible request JSON keys with underscores when forwarding to llama.cpp.
rules.title: Store canonical DB keys and OpenAI JSON keys
rules.why: Internal canonicalization and the external OpenAI-compatible API use different naming conventions.

topics.condition: When operating or troubleshooting Dispatcher serve/bench/eval commands, debug endpoints, CLI overrides, database views, or detailed parameter naming, consult the README operating reference.
topics.title: Dispatcher operating reference
